criteria.name: Problem passes the swap-test
criteria.rationale: The field names a specific customer and a specific failure: "Marisol runs the front desk at Riverbend — six therapists, one site," twenty patients to re-book when a therapist calls out, "About seven of those twenty end up with someone who isn't credentialed," and the concrete instance of "a vestibular patient sitting down with the sports-ortho therapist." The quote "I book the day twice" and the discovery mechanism (the therapist walks out mid-session) are not text any competitor could claim word for word.

criteria.name: Appetite is a fixed tier
criteria.rationale: The field reads "Small (≤2 weeks)" — the value is the fixed small tier, with the parenthetical stating the tier's ceiling rather than a duration estimated for this particular project. It is not a calendar estimate (no "about three weeks," no per-project range or contingency), so the tier is doing the work and the parenthetical only defines it.

criteria.name: Solution sketch under-specified and within cap
criteria.rationale: The sketch runs roughly 94 words, well inside the ~150 cap. It is prose only — no diagrams, no acceptance criteria, and no edge-case enumeration; it states the shape (read the existing credentialing file, map the plan-of-care condition code, surface only credentialed replacement slots) plus two boundaries ("Marisol still confirms every move by hand"; initial evaluations untouched) without specifying mechanics.

criteria.name: Every assumption passes the falsifiability checklist
criteria.rationale: The one recorded assumption has all four sub-fields and each holds: the claim is quantified as an action driving a measurable outcome ("Filtering the reschedule list by credentialed specialty takes mismatched re-bookings from about 7 in 20 down to under 2 in 20"); the threshold is a pre-committed kill line ("Still above 4 in 20 after the first month... and I stop") that reality could land on either side of, so it is not can't-fail and is not a preference about the document; and the test mines data already held ("the 340 reschedule moves in Riverbend's existing last-quarter export... No build required, about an hour") with a "by when" of "By Friday." The threshold is stated in post-launch terms while the cheap test is retrospective, but the checklist requires a cheap timeboxed test rather than one that measures the threshold directly, and the export test does bear on the claim's premise.
